text: In an Echo State Network, why are the input-to-reservoir weights W_in and the reservoir-to-reservoir weights W typically kept fixed after initialisation?
choices: Training both W_in and W simultaneously is computationally intractable
Only the readout weights W_out need to be trained, making the system a linear regression problem
Reservoir weights must be sparse to satisfy the echo state property
Fixed weights ensure the reservoir operates in the edge-of-chaos regime automatically
explanation: The key insight of ESNs is to only train the readout weights W_out via linear regression (e.g. ridge regression), while the reservoir weights remain fixed. This avoids the backpropagation-through-time problems of trained RNNs. The fixed recurrent weights project inputs into a high-dimensional nonlinear feature space; the readout merely finds a linear combination of these features — a convex optimisation with a unique global solution.
